summary: The 52-episode TV series adapts the first four of the manga's five parts, ch1-~205 of 242 (v1-v19 of 22); the fifth part, 'Kikan-hen' / Program Bandersnatch (ch210-242), is never adapted. Season 1 (eps 1-26) is a clean, near-linear 2-4 chapters-per-episode run over ch1-77, and the season break falls exactly on the v7 finale ch77 (the departure for America), which is also the manga's part-two boundary - the single most load-bearing anchor here. Season 2 covers part three (ch78-110) over eps 27-36 at a similar rate, then compresses the whole 99-chapter Alice arc (ch111-209) into eps 37-50 with genuine restructuring: the Keith Violet / March Hare fight (ch~186-190) is pulled forward to ep 44 before the island infiltration, and Keith Silver is killed off early at Gallows Bell (eps 33-34) where the manga keeps him alive until inside the Karion Tower (ch180-183). Eps 51-52 are an anime-original wrap that kills Keith White, who is alive and the villain of the unadapted fifth part in the manga, so they are annotated rather than anchored. The chapter space itself had to be rebuilt: Shogakukan's per-volume TOCs (via Kinokuniya) and MangaDex agree chapter-for-chapter on all 22 volumes at 242 chapters, one more than the AniList figure our entry carries. Finally, stored episode 53 'PS2 Video Game' is not an episode at all - it is an animefillerlist row we imported verbatim, and it holds the series' only existing anchor.

Compresses the rest of Tillinghast's Egrigori exposition (v12, ch128-132) and the opening of the Alice arc (v13) down to the Drakken Corps material: ch136 離反 Betrayer and ch137 竜隊（ドラッケン）= ep title, closing on ch138 決断. Arc-span derivation.

The Alice flashback episode. Ch139 証明 / ch140 始源（オリジネーター）/ ch141 誕生 = ep title 誕生（アリス）/ ch142 成長 / ch143 青花（ブルーウィッシュ）(the blue roses) and all of v14 (ch144-154), which Shogakukan's own v14 blurb describes as Alice's escape attempt and the slaughter of the test children - exactly this episode's content. Arrival at the Karion Fortress island = ch162 Fortress (v15); Takeshi rejoins; Black's dining-room reveal and the wall that separates the party = ch166 陥穽 Snare, the first chapter of v16, which Shogakukan's v16 blurb names as the start of the Karion Tower infiltration. v15 has no publisher TOC on Kinokuniya; titles from MangaDex.

Ch193 激震; Keith White resurrected inside Black's body = ch194 帰還（リザレクション）Resurrection; ep title 黙示（リベレイション）= ch195 Revelations; ch196 地上 / ch197 激突; the Jabberwock merging with Black Alice = ch198 侵食（エンクローチメント）, the v18 finale.

Independently, MangaUpdates records the anime's coverage as ending at 'Vol 19, Chap 205'.

annotations.note: The Keith Violet / March Hare fight is pulled forward: the anime stages it on the bridge BEFORE the island, while Shogakukan's v18 blurb places it at the head of v18 (after Silver's defeat), with the identical beat of Hayato fully synchronising with the Knight to save Ryo. Ep title 幻境（アルカディア）= ch186.

The anime kills Keith Silver / the Mad Hatter at Gallows Bell (ch100-102 material). In the manga Silver survives Gallows Bell and is only defeated inside the Karion Tower (ch180 銀光（シルバー）/ ch181 戦鬼（マッドハッター）/ ch182 溶融 / ch183 炎熱, per the v17 TOC and the v18 blurb's 'having only just defeated Keith Silver').

Roughly 34 chapters (v12-v14: Tillinghast's exposition, Takeshi's journey through Alice's world, the full Alice backstory) are compressed into three episodes and partly re-ordered. Interior chapter boundaries in this stretch are not individually attestable.
First half is an anime-original clip-show recap of season 1 (the four Keiths reviewing events); only the back half adapts new material.
In the manga the Jabberwock/Alice giant appears over NEW YORK and a runaway nuclear missile is the crisis (Shogakukan v19 blurb). The anime relocates the same climax to the Karion Fortress island.

The anime finished on 2002-03-30, three weeks before the manga ended, and wraps with an original resolution: Keith Blue and Keith White kill each other (Dormouse vs Humpty Dumpty). In the manga Keith White SURVIVES the Alice arc and is the antagonist of the unadapted fifth part, 'Kikan-hen' (ch210-242, Program Bandersnatch). MangaUpdates puts the anime's coverage end at ch205, so eps 51-52 are left unanchored rather than pushed to ch209.

repairs.why: Episode 53 is not an episode. Both seasons total 52 (26 + 26) per en.wikipedia, ja.wikipedia and the two AniList components in the context file. The stored row 53 'PS2 Video Game' is an animefillerlist artifact - AFL's own table carries a 53rd row literally titled 'PS2 Video Game' dated 2002-03-28, and our row reproduces it verbatim including the type 'Mixed Canon/Filler'. The mu-derived anchor 205/v19 attached to it comes from MangaUpdates' series field anime.end = 'Vol 19, Chap 205', which describes the anime's END, not a 53rd episode. Recommend deleting the anchor (and, separately, the row); the ch205 datum is carried here on ep 50 where the content evidence independently lands.

structure.notes:
CHAPTER SPACE. The manga runs 242 numbered chapters in 22 tankoubon; the context file's AniList total_chapters=241 is one short. Volume boundaries were rebuilt from Shogakukan's own per-volume tables of contents (the '出版社内容情報' block on Kinokuniya's product pages, which lists every 第N話 in the volume) for 19 of the 22 volumes, and cross-checked chapter-for-chapter against MangaDex's chapter feed for all 22: ZERO mismatches. Boundaries used throughout: v1 1-10, v2 11-21, v3 22-32, v4 33-43, v5 44-54, v6 55-65, v7 66-77, v8 78-88, v9 89-99, v10 100-110, v11 111-121, v12 122-132, v13 133-143, v14 144-154, v15 155-165, v16 166-176, v17 177-187, v18 188-198, v19 199-209, v20 210-220, v21 221-231, v22 232-242. Kinokuniya's blurbs for v3, v4 and v15 are truncated (no TOC), so those three volumes rest on MangaDex plus the arithmetic pinned by the two neighbouring publisher TOCs. Note the trap: a prior pass on this series dropped v10's first chapter (火神（アグニ）) from the same blurb and came out with 241 chapters and every volume from 10 on shifted by one.

SEASONS. 52 episodes, not 53: PROJECT ARMS eps 1-26 (2001-04-07..09-29) and PROJECT ARMS: The 2nd Chapter eps 27-52 (2001-10-06..2002-03-30). Our cumulative numbering already matches Wikipedia's overall numbering 1-52 one-for-one. Row 53 'PS2 Video Game' is an animefillerlist artifact and is not an episode - see repairs.

ADAPTATION SHAPE. Season 1 (eps 1-26) covers exactly the manga's first two parts, ch1-77 = v1-v7, at a steady 2-4 chapters per episode, and the season break lands precisely on the v7 finale (ch77 離陸 Take Off, the departure for America). Season 2 accelerates hard: eps 27-36 cover part three (ch78-110 = v8-v10) at ~3-4 chapters an episode, then eps 37-50 compress the whole of part four (ch111-209 = v11-v19) at 5-16 chapters an episode with real re-ordering. The manga's fifth part, 'Kikan-hen' (ch210-242, v20-v22, Program Bandersnatch), is NOT adapted at all. The manga's part boundaries in chapter space: part 1 'Kakusei-hen' 1-32, part 2 'Kaikou-hen' 33-77, part 3 'Shinka-hen' 78-110, part 4 'Alice-hen' 111-209, part 5 'Kikan-hen' 210-242.

TITLE TRAP. Anime episode titles are frequently, but not always, lifted from a chapter inside the episode - and the show reuses chapter titles out of position (ep 29 is titled 闘士（ハンター）, which is ch86, but its content is ch81-84; ep 51 青空（ブルーウィッシュ） echoes ch143 青花 which was already animated at ep 42). It also splices two adjacent chapters into one title twice: ep 33 火神（マーズ） = ch100's kanji + ch99's reading, ep 50 世界（アニムス） = ch205's kanji + ch204's reading. Every anchor here was made on episode-summary content, with the title match as corroboration only.

STORED TITLES. Our episode titles are AFL's English set and differ cosmetically from Wikipedia's for eps 27 (Arrive/Alive), 29 (Hunter/Hunted), 40 (Reverse/Rebirth), 48 (Humans/Human), 50 (Existence/Animus), 52 (Departure/Life). Same episodes; no repair proposed.

flags_for_sean: Row 53 'PS2 Video Game' is not an episode (animefillerlist artifact reproduced verbatim, including its Mixed type). It currently holds the series' ONLY anchor (205/v19, source mu). Proposed repair deletes that anchor; the row itself probably wants deleting too, and aired_episodes/total_episodes want 53 -> 52.

Manga chapter count: sources say 242 (MangaDex lastChapter=242 and the summed publisher TOCs), the context file carries AniList total_chapters=241, and ja.wikipedia's infobox says 243. The volume arithmetic is independently double-verified at 242, so 241 is likely one short. Not proposed as a repair because it is an entry-level field, not an anchor.

Eps 51-52 deliberately left unanchored. MangaUpdates places the anime's coverage end at ch205 (which ep 50 reaches), while the two episodes' content loosely parallels ch206-209 and then resolves with an anime-original Blue-vs-White duel that contradicts the manga (White survives into the unadapted fifth part). AFL types ep 51 as Manga Canon and ep 52 as Mixed; I could not source a retype to anime-only-canon with two independent sources, so no type_correction is proposed - flagging for Sean instead.

Ep 44 is unanchored on purpose: its content (Keith Violet / March Hare, ch~186-190) is out of running order relative to eps 45-49, so an anchor there would break monotonicity. Recorded as a 'rearranged' annotation instead.
Eps 43 and 46 left unanchored - no evidence I could source pinned their boundaries; they interpolate between the ep 42 (154) and ep 45 (166), and ep 45 (166) and ep 47 (177) anchors.

Ep 47 END is 176 or 177 (a volume-crossing one-chapter ambiguity: ch176 中枢（ピボット） matches 'central processing unit', but Shogakukan's v17 blurb puts Tillinghast shooting Dewey and the self-destruct at the head of v17). Chose 177; flagging.

Ep 33 END is 99 or 100 for the same reason (the ep title splices both). Chose 99 so that ch100 火神（アグニ）- which Shogakukan names as v10's first chapter, with Silver's flames and Takeshi's transformation - opens ep 34, matching ep 34's summary.
